body.objective: Make the documented stale-shared-index artifact of isolated Science Forge commits safe and intelligible. After an isolated-index commit advances HEAD without touching the process-global index, raw `git status` can display a newly committed path simultaneously as a staged deletion and an untracked addition. This is technically expected but operationally dangerous: resident agents may attempt reset/restore cleanup or a manual commit may absorb misleading index state.
body.stop_condition: Add a read-only `s-f git status` or equivalent coordinator/worker surface that computes HEAD-to-worktree truth independently of a stale shared index, reports the shared-index base/digest and whether it is stale, distinguishes real staged intent from post-isolated-commit artifacts, and prints exact safe next actions. Add a bounded reconciliation command only if it can prove by compare-and-swap that no concurrent staged intent is lost: preserve every genuine staged blob and stage/unstage bit, rebase it onto current HEAD or refuse with a typed conflict, and never touch unstaged/untracked files. Integrate the health finding into `s-f overview`, `work check`, `work commit` and generated AGENTS/CLAUDE guidance. Add deterministic two-agent regressions for: clean index plus isolated commit; concurrent genuine staged edits; the same path committed through the isolated index while present in the old shared index; HEAD advancing twice; and a manual raw-git attempt that receives a loud warning. The safe status must remain fast on the current large repository.
body.forbid: no `git reset`, `git read-tree HEAD` or index replacement that can discard another agent's staged intent; no broad add/commit; no rewriting commits; no treating staged entries as owned merely because they are under one work item's allowlist; no hiding true conflicts; no requirement that all agents serialize behind one global lock; no mutation from the read-only status command
notes: Live recurrence on 2026-07-20: after atomic isolated-index planning commits, raw status showed `D  planning/work-items/quantum-dressed-canonical-berezinian-locality-preflight.json` and `??` for the same existing file because HEAD advanced while the shared index remained at its old tree.

The risk became concrete minutes later: raw coordination commit 032aa6c70, which has no Science Forge WORK_COMMITTED receipt, unintentionally deleted nine unrelated selected-action work items/events already present in parent 244791802. Exact blobs were restored in 8a8fb31c8. This does not show that `s-f work commit` violated its isolated-index guarantee; it shows that leaving an apparently ordinary but stale raw index available as an unguarded escape hatch can still corrupt concurrent planning history.
The SF5 guarantee that isolated commits read/write the shared index zero times is correct and must be preserved; this request addresses the user-facing consequence rather than weakening isolation.
A per-agent persistent index or virtual status layer is acceptable if raw-Git escape hatches are documented and guarded.
